data.summary: Microscopist on 4 field(s): density lower vs DMSO; 8 observations; candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors, unknown

observations.finding: Markedly fewer cells per field vs DMSO; cultures sparse with large gaps vs confluent monolayer control.
Mean nuclear size increased with high fraction of very large nuclei vs small uniform ovals in DMSO.
Nuclei irregular, lobulated and non-round with reduced circularity and solidity vs smooth oval DMSO nuclei. Blue DNA appears as clustered puntcate / fragmented lobes within enlarged nuclear area.
Increased apparent multinucleation / polyploidy: many cells contain multiple DNA masses or single giant polyploid nucleus vs single nucleus per cell in DMSO.
DNA content per nuclear object increased (brighter and larger DAPI masses) vs DMSO.
F-actin (red) more intense and heterogeneous: thick cortical rims / stress fibers in spread large cells vs thin cortical actin in DMSO; increased actin-to-tubulin ratio and texture variance.

Frequent bright yellow-white rounded cells (overlap of blue DNA + green tubulin + red actin) consistent with condensed mitotic chromosomes / failed divisions; isolated bright debris. No direct feature for mitotic figures provided.

Beta-tubulin (green) not lost: diffuse cytoplasmic green remains, with bright perichromosomal signal in rounded cells; not consistent with wholesale microtubule depolymerization. No microtubule-loss feature in top deviations.

notable_cells.why: example low-density field with enlarged lobulated blue nuclei vs dense DMSO control field f_9fbcadfb9d0d
large cells with clustered punctate DNA lobes and thick red actin cortex illustrating irregular nuclear morphology
giant polyploid cell with multiple DNA masses at 3.0 uM, same phenotype as 0.3 uM

candidate_mechanisms.why: Combination of decreased cell count (z -12.3/-12.7, 85/78 vs 311 DMSO), strongly decreased nuc form_factor (z -49.9/-31.7, 0.828/0.86 vs 0.917) and solidity (z -48.3/-33.0, 0.952/0.959 vs 0.972), increased frac_large_nucleus (z 22.7/14.1, 0.104/0.069 vs 0.013), increased frac_multinucleate_proxy (z 14.7/11.7, 0.58/0.51 vs 0.268) and increased nuc_dna_integrated (z 11.5, 579 vs 291) indicates failed cytokinesis/polyploidy; persistent at 0.3 and 3.0 uM with elevated act_std (z 14.7/21.3) and act_tub_ratio (z 12.1/13.3) from cell spreading, classic Aurora inhibition mitotic failure phenotype.

report.uncertainty: Eg5 inhibitors and Microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers also cause mitotic failure and polyploidy and cannot be fully excluded from composite alone, but Aurora kinase inhibitors best matches extreme loss of nuclear roundness/solidity plus high multinucleation and DNA content increase with retained tubulin and high cortical actin; no actin loss to support Actin disruptors, no simple DNA damage fragmentation pattern.

what_was_wrong: describe_phenotype on 4 fields: density lower vs DMSO, 8 observations, candidates Aurora kinase inhibitors, unknown (e4) - visually plausible because Aurora B inhibition also gives large irregular nuclei/polyploidy. This misled hypothesis board to retain Aurora 0.12 (e14) but correctly not overruled NSC. Should have weighted that microscopy alone cannot distinguish cytokinesis failure vs spindle depolymerization multinucleation.

k-neighbour 3/10 Protein synthesis in both atlas votes (e5, e8) - expected noise: mitotic arrest reduces cell size/translation secondarily; agent correctly kept probability 0.03 and contradicted with e2/e4.

## Hypothesis history

- after step 14: Microtubule destabilizers 0.82, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.12, Protein synthesis 0.03, Eg5 inhibitors 0.02, DNA damage 0.01, Microtubule stabilizers 0.01

## Conclusion

**Microtubule destabilizers** (stated probability 0.82); key evidence e8, e5, e2, e6, e4.

Why: NSC 4/4 votes microtubule destabilizers at 0.95-0.97 similarity across doses, consistent with extreme nuclear irregularity and polyploidy; microscopist Aurora suggestion not enough independent evidence to override high-similarity 1-NN prio…

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Live mitotic timing + anti-tubulin immunofluorescence at 0.03-0.1 µM vs vincristine and alisertib controls: quantify mitotic index, monopolar/bipolar spindles, and tubulin polymer mass to distinguish microtubule depolymerization from Aurora B cytokinesis failure; add phospho-Histone H3 flow.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Clean on-target call: 4/4 atlas votes for vincristine-class at 0.95-0.97 with flat dose-response saturation across 0.03-3 uM; actin and nuclear signatures replicate. Local PI plating notes for CYTO-ID-type readouts not in evidence do not override direct atlas + measured tubulin loss.

## Unblinding

Compound: **demecolcine** (PubChem CID [220401](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/220401))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **Microtubule destabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Microtubule destabilizers**.

## Reflection

Blinded NSC run, 8-dose demecolcine (0.003-10 uM) - verdict approve/correct. Truth microtubule destabilizers, agent 0.82, calibrated leave 0.12 for Aurora.

What was right:
- Phenotype signal was extreme and reproduced across acquisitions: w_13173fc040 0.3 uM nuc_form_factor z -49.9, nuc_solidity -48.3, frac_large_nucleus +22.8 (e2); w_c4bb8c8ab5 3 uM nuc_solidity -33.0, nuc_form_factor -31.7 (e3); w_17353b8062 0.03 uM nuc_solidity -69.9, nuc_form_factor -49.9 (e6); w_4134b8c5f2 0.1 uM nuc_solidity -62.8, nuc_form_factor -51.5 (e7). - Atlas comparison got it right twice: NSC 2/2 microtubule destabilizers (e5) then 4/4 after expanding dose coverage (e8), k-neighbour 7/10 microtubule destabilizers, 3/10 Protein synthesis. Agent used this as prior in update_hypotheses 0.82 vs 0.12 Aurora, 0.03 protein synthesis (e14) and conclusion p=0.82 (e15). Review critique correctly notes flat saturation 0.03-3 uM similarity 0.95-0.97 - our 4 wells sampled 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 3 uM captured onset at low dose already saturated (e6 -69.9 at 0.03 uM not weaker than e3 -33.0 at 3 uM).
- Unblinding check justified reliance on phenotype: lookup demecolcine CID 220401 CHEMBL312862 mechanisms none curated, name and BBBC021 structure agree (e16, e17). No database MoA to lean on, so phenotype-only call was appropriate.
- Literature after unblinding supports call: colcemid/colcemid resistance via tubulin mutations PMID 17938271, mutations stabilizing microtubules conferring colcemid/vinblastine resistance PMID 12883031, and early work on colcemid centriole cycle effects PMID 7200989, consistent with colcemid/demecolcine as tubulin depolymerizer/microtubule destabilizer.

What was wrong or missed:
- describe_phenotype on 4 fields: density lower vs DMSO, 8 observations, candidates Aurora kinase inhibitors, unknown (e4) - visually plausible because Aurora B inhibition also gives large irregular nuclei/polyploidy. This misled hypothesis board to retain Aurora 0.12 (e14) but correctly not overruled NSC. Should have weighted that microscopy alone cannot distinguish cytokinesis failure vs spindle depolymerization multinucleation.
- k-neighbour 3/10 Protein synthesis in both atlas votes (e5, e8) - expected noise: mitotic arrest reduces cell size/translation secondarily; agent correctly kept probability 0.03 and contradicted with e2/e4.
- Dose_response tests were underpowered and flat, not informative but could have misled if overinterpreted: nuc_form_factor rho +0.80 p=0.2 (e9), frac_large_nucleus rho +0.40 p=0.6 (e10), tub_mean rho +0.40 p=0.6 (e11), frac_mitotic_like rho -0.11 p=0.89 (e12), cell_count rho -0.80 p=0.2 (e13). n=4 wells, all p >=0.2. e11 in particular does not show tubulin loss trend expected for destabilizers, contradicting review summary of tubulin loss; agent correctly did not down-weight destabilizers on this single noisy feature and kept act_std +21.3 (e3), +23.8 (e6) and act_tub_ratio +17.9 (e7) as cytoskeletal dysregulation supporting destabilizer rather than Aurora.

Proposed next experiment: As proposed (e15 next_experiment_if_this_were_a_real_lab): live mitotic timing + anti-tubulin IF at 0.03-0.1 uM vs vincristine and alisertib controls, quantifying mitotic index, monopolar/bipolar spindles, polymer mass, plus pHH3 flow - directly separates microtubule depolymerization from Aurora cytokinesis failure without relying on nuclear shape alone.
